drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (not quantified in data but implied by high Z4 % and low Z1 % this month vs 43% Z1 last month)

ACWR likely elevated: this month’s 23.8 km in 5 runs (4.76 km/run) vs last month’s 51.3 km in 10 runs (5.13 km/run) — but acute load concentrated in fewer, harder sessions (37% Z4 this month vs 8% last month)
Resting HR trend not provided, but avg HR increased from 134 to 144 bpm across months while pace slowed slightly — suggesting autonomic strain
Sleep, HRV, and body battery metrics are absent — critical gaps, but absence + pattern of elevated HR + high-intensity skew implies insufficient recovery
readiness.guidance: This week must prioritize restoration over volume or intensity — even if the calendar shows 'room' for more running.

monthly_review.summary: September shows a sharp shift toward higher-intensity work with reduced aerobic base support, occurring alongside declining volume and cadence — inconsistent with sustainable progression given missing recovery metrics.
monthly_review.highlight: The jump from 8% Z4 time last month to 37% Z4 this month — without corresponding improvement in VO2max (stable at ~39–42) or efficiency — signals disproportionate stress without adaptation payoff.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km would require 27.5 km across 5 remaining sessions — an average of 5.5 km/session, but current readiness is compromised and recent Z4 load is already excessive; chasing this number risks maladaptation and is not advisable.

insights.title: Z4 dominance without performance gain
insights.body: Z4 time surged from 8% (Aug) to 37% (Sep), yet best pace improved only marginally (453 → 369 sec/km) and VO2max remained stable (39–42); meanwhile, cadence dropped 15 spm and efficiency worsened — indicating fatigue-mediated form breakdown, not fitness gain.

insights.title: Cadence collapse correlates with high-intensity concentration
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 134 spm (Sep), and the two slowest, highest-HR runs (Sep 6: 158 bpm, 90 spm; Sep 10: 134 bpm, 138 spm) show the steepest cadence drops — suggesting neuromuscular fatigue overriding technique under load.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling worsening with intensity shift
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose from 2.6 (Aug) to 3.0 (Sep), and the longest run (10.7 km on Sep 6) showed 5.0 — above the 5% threshold — confirming aerobic system strain during sustained efforts, despite no VO2max increase.

insights.title: Pace-HR dissociation signals autonomic cost
insights.body: Avg pace improved (+11 sec/km) while avg HR rose (+10 bpm) — a rare inverse relationship suggesting compensatory effort due to reduced parasympathetic reserve, especially given missing HRV/sleep data.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤128 bpm, 45 min, Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Restores aerobic stimulus without adding sympathetic load; matches Aug’s lowest avg HR (128 bpm) and supports TE recovery

recommendations.action: Complete rest or non-impact mobility only (e.g., foam roll + diaphragmatic breathing, 20 min), Thursday
recommendations.reason: Critical to interrupt accumulating Z4 stress; cadence and TE deterioration indicate need for neural reset

recommendations.action: Zone 2 tempo, HR 130–135 bpm, 35 min, Saturday — stop immediately if cadence falls below 142 spm
recommendations.reason: Re-establishes rhythm and efficiency guardrail; 142 spm is the minimum observed in non-Z4 runs (e.g., Aug 21: 148 spm @ 133 bpm)

risk_flags.evidence: 37% Z4 time (vs 8% last month), +10 bpm avg HR, +0.4 aerobic TE, cadence drop of 15 spm, no VO2max gain
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z4/Z5 work for ≥10 days; reassess after 3 consecutive Zone 1–2 sessions with stable cadence ≥145 spm

risk_flags.evidence: Stride length spiked to 101.8 cm (Sep 3) and ground contact rose to 389 ms (Sep 1) — both extremes — while vertical oscillillation increased to 9.2 cm (Sep 3), suggesting instability under fatigue
risk_flags.action: Eliminate all speedwork until stride metrics normalize to <95 cm stride, <330 ms ground contact, and <8.0 cm vertical oscillation

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic control and movement efficiency before reintroducing intensity — prioritizing cadence consistency, HR discipline, and decoupling containment.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 tempo with cadence biofeedback (≥142 spm mandatory)
